newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU urges reforms to save Bulgarian economy.
newsitem.headline: EU urges reforms to save Bulgarian economy.

text.p: The European Union on Monday called for swift reforms in Bulgaria to try and rescue the economy which has plunged into hyper-inflation.
"The European Union wishes to express its deep concern at recent events in Bulgaria," the Dutch foreign ministry, and acting EU president, said in a brief statement.
"Rapid and effective structural reforms are urgently necessary in order to secure the recovery of the economy."
The statement encouraged all political parties to support recently-elected President Petar Stoyanov's attempts to find compromise solutions, including a date for elections.
"The EU calls upon all political forces to work together to overcome the present deadlock and to restore the confidence of the Bulgarian people in the democratic institutions," it said.
Thousands of protesters marched through Sofia on Sunday to demand a general election but the ex-communist Socialist party insisted it would form a new cabinet.
The Socialists plan to form a government under Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev, but opponents blame him for recent clashes between police and demonstrators which sparked days of street protests.

The constitution requires Stoyanov to ask the Socialists, the biggest parliamentary party, to form a government, but the president, elected only last Wednesday, has said the government would be unlikely to win public confidence.
The economic plight has meant huge price volatility forcing shops to close and curbing the purchase of all but the most basic foods.
